why_this_tool: MLflow is the one tool here that keeps the evaluation dataset, the metrics, the baseline comparison, the threshold verdict and the registered model version in the same store, so a release gate can be recorded and audited where promotion happens.
alternatives: Evidently generates drift and quality test reports but has no model registry; Great Expectations validates data assumptions and not model quality; CheckList generates behavioral test cases for NLP models only; plain pytest with scikit-learn metrics gives full control but keeps no run history or verdict attached to a model version; Locust load-tests a serving endpoint and nothing else.

steps.why: Default accuracy rarely matches what the business decides on. A gate is only useful when the gated number is the one that drives the promote or block decision.

steps.why: A regression suite only means something when the data does not move between releases. Tracking the dataset gives every result a digest that proves which data was scored.

steps.do: Run a dataset evaluation on precomputed predictions once per slice, such as one run per customer segment or class, with the slice name recorded as a run tag.
steps.done_when: The experiment holds one evaluation run per slice, each with its own metric values and slice tag.

source.title: ML Model Evaluation | MLflow AI Platform

steps.why: An aggregate score can improve while one segment gets worse. Evaluating stored predictions per slice makes those regressions visible without reloading the model.

steps.do: Query the runs programmatically to pull the candidate and baseline metrics for every slice into one table, and compare them side by side.
steps.done_when: You have a table listing candidate and baseline values of your decision metric for each slice, built only from the tracking server.

steps.why: The gate must read persisted results, not numbers from a notebook cell. This query is what an automated check will later run.

steps.do: Write a behavioral test with function evaluation: wrap the model in a Python function that perturbs inputs in a way that should not change the answer, and evaluate it with a custom metric counting changed predictions.
steps.done_when: A run records an invariance failure rate metric, and it rises when you make the perturbation harsher.

source.title: ML Model Evaluation | MLflow AI Platform

steps.why: Held-out accuracy does not tell you whether the model is stable under harmless input changes. Function evaluation lets you score any callable, so invariance and directional tests fit the same tracking flow.

steps.do: Run model validation on the candidate's evaluation result with metric thresholds: an absolute floor on the decision metric and a minimum improvement over the baseline's result.
steps.done_when: Validation passes for the candidate and raises a validation failure when you swap in the weaker model.

source.title: ML Model Evaluation | MLflow AI Platform

steps.why: This turns good enough into a pass or fail that code can act on. Comparing against the baseline is what makes the suite a regression check and not only a quality bar.
